_comment: Google Cloud service catalogue for the services widget. Hand-curated for the
same reason as azure_services.json: there is no botocore equivalent, and
deriving names from post text produced 'That', 'Correct' and 'Operation'.
A generous list is safe -- only services actually detected in a GCP post are
rendered -- but a WRONG name is not, because it would match ordinary prose and
inflate every count. So bare words are avoided: 'Cloud Run' and 'Cloud Storage'
are specific enough, 'Projects', 'Folders' and 'APIs' are not services at all.
'Resource Manager' appears in both this file and azure_services.json, naming
two different products. That is safe because detection is scoped per cloud:
the Azure catalogue is only ever matched against Azure posts and this one only
against GCP posts, so neither can borrow the other's count.
url points at cloud.google.com. Docs pages under /*/docs/* now 301 to
overview pages are used here rather than deep doc links.

Cloud Identity.desc: Google's identity service holding the users and groups that IAM policies reference.

Google Workspace.desc: The productivity suite whose directory doubles as an identity source for Google Cloud.

Resource Manager.desc: The API that creates and organises organisations, folders and projects.

Service Usage.desc: Enables and disables APIs on a project, and lists what is currently enabled.

Cloud IAM.desc: Grants roles on resources, inherited down the organisation, folder and project hierarchy.

Cloud Run.desc: Serverless containers that scale to zero, with request- and instance-based billing.

App Engine.desc: Managed application platform with standard and flexible runtime environments.

Compute Engine.desc: Virtual machines, with machine families, custom types and committed use discounts.

Google Kubernetes Engine.desc: Managed Kubernetes with Standard and Autopilot modes.

Cloud Functions.desc: Event-driven functions, now delivered on the Cloud Run infrastructure.

Cloud Storage.desc: Object storage with Standard, Nearline, Coldline and Archive classes.

BigQuery.desc: Serverless data warehouse, billed by bytes scanned or by reserved slots.

Cloud SQL.desc: Managed MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server instances.

Cloud Spanner.desc: Horizontally scalable relational database with external consistency.

Firestore.desc: Serverless document database with real-time listeners.

Pub/Sub.desc: Asynchronous messaging with topics, subscriptions and at-least-once delivery.

Cloud Logging.desc: Log ingestion, routing through sinks, and retention.

Cloud Monitoring.desc: Metrics, dashboards, uptime checks and alerting policies.

Cloud KMS.desc: Managed encryption keys, with software, HSM and external protection levels.

Secret Manager.desc: Versioned store for secrets, with IAM-controlled access per secret.

Cloud DNS.desc: Managed authoritative DNS, public and private zones.

Cloud Load Balancing.desc: Global and regional load balancing across backends.

Cloud Build.desc: Managed build service that runs steps in containers.

Artifact Registry.desc: Stores container images and language packages, with per-repository IAM.

Vertex AI.desc: Managed platform for training, tuning and serving models, including Gemini.

Cloud Armor.desc: WAF and DDoS protection in front of Cloud Load Balancing.

Container OS.desc: Google's minimal container-optimised operating system for GKE and Compute Engine nodes.
